fact_en:
How do doctors see your bones without cutting you open?

They use X-rays! These rays pass through soft body tissue but get absorbed by denser bones, creating pictures of the bones inside your body!
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagkita sa mga doktor sa imong mga bukog nga dili ka gisi-on?

Naggamit sila ug X-rays! Makaagi ang mga rays sa humok nga unod sa lawas apan masuhop sa mas baga nga bukog, mao nga makahimo ug litrato sa mga bukog sulod sa lawas!
evidence: "X-ray Buto" reads as "X-ray explosion" in Cebuano — the card is about seeing bones, which its own body and terms give as "bukog".

fact_en:
How do valuable minerals like gold form deep underground?

Valuable minerals like gold formed deep underground! They were created by intense heat and heavy pressure inside the Earth.
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagporma sa mahal nga mineral sama sa bulawan ilalom sa yuta?

Naporma ang mahal nga mineral sama sa bulawan ilalom sa yuta! Nahimo kini tungod sa init ug presyur sulod sa Kalibutan.
evidence: "Pagtapak" means stepping on (or patching), not forming — the card explains how gold forms underground (body: "naporma"/"nahimo"), so the headline names a different action.

fact_en:
What animals live in mangrove forests?

Many animals call it home! Birds, crabs, oysters, and shellfish cling to the mangrove roots.
fact_bis:
Unsa nga mga hayop ang nagpuyo sa kabakhawan?

Daghang hayop ang nagtawag niini nga pinuy-anan! Ang mga langgam, alimango, talaba, ug kinhason mokapyot sa mga gamot sa bakhaw.
evidence: Last word "Mangrov" is cut off; the card itself contains "Mangrove".

fact_en:
What does the color of sand tell us?

The color tells you its secret source! It shows exactly what kind of rock or shell the sand came from.
fact_bis:
Unsay isulti sa kolor sa balas?

Isulti sa kolor ang ginikanan niini! Ipakita niini kung unsang klase sa bato o kabhang kini naggikan.
evidence: Title ends on a bare particle with its head noun missing.

fact_en: Earth spins from west to east! That's why the Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west — it's actually us who are turning!
fact_bis: Molibot ang Earth gikan sa kasadpan paingon sa sidlakan! Mao nga morag mosubang ang Adlaw sa sidlakan ug mosalop sa kasadpan — kita man diay ang nagtuyok, dili ang Adlaw!
evidence: Cebuano "tirok" means to gather/assemble, not to spin (body correctly uses "nagtuyok"/"molibot"), and the dangling "pakadto" leaves the headline both wrong and unfinished.

fact_en:
Does every dead animal become a fossil?

Not every dead animal becomes a fossil! It happens only rarely, which makes each fossil very precious.
fact_bis:
Mahimong fossil ba ang tanang patay nga hayop?

Dili tanang patay nga hayop mahimong fossil! Talagsaon ra kini, mao nga bililhon kaayo ang matag fossil.
evidence: "Bihag" means captive/hostage in Cebuano; the card says fossilization is rare (body: "talagsaon"), so "Bihag Ra Fossil" names a captive rather than rarity.

fact_en:
What does Mercury's surface look like?

It's covered with craters — big bowl-shaped holes like the Moon, made by space rocks that crashed into it long ago!
fact_bis:
Unsay dagway sa nawong sa Mercury?

Puno kini sa mga crater — dagkong buho nga sama sa Bulan, gibuhat sa mga bato sa kawanangan nga nahagba niini kaniadto!
evidence: Last word "Mercur" is cut off; the card itself contains "Mercury".

fact_en: Because Talc is super soft, rubbing it on paper leaves a thin white mark like chalk! It wipes off easily since its sheets break apart.
fact_bis: Tungod kay humok kaayo ang Talc, kung imo kining kuskuson sa papel, mabilin ang nipis nga puti nga marka sama sa tisa! Sayon ra mawala kay nagkabulag ang mga panid niini.
evidence: "Lumot" is moss/algae in Cebuano (102 corpus bodies use it that way, incl. 5 inside soft-cards where it still means moss), while this card is about talc being humok, so the headline reads "Moss Talc Paper".

fact_en:
Why do stage shows use soft shadows?

They use the soft penumbra to make shadows gentle instead of sharp! This makes the scene look pleasant and easy on the eyes.
fact_bis:
Nganong naggamit og humok nga landong ang mga stage show?

Gigamit nila ang hanap nga penumbra aron mahimong humok ang landong! Mao nga mas nindot tan-awon ug dili makapakurat sa mata.
evidence: "Lumos" is drown/smother in Cebuano — the corpus's single body use is "lumos sa siga" (smother a flame) — and the body itself says "humok nga landong", so the headline reads "Drowned Shadow on Stage".

fact_en:
How do black holes form?

Very massive stars can collapse into a black hole after a supernova! Its gravity is so strong that not even light can escape its boundary, called the event horizon.
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagporma sa mga black hole?

Ang kaayo ka dagko nga mga bituin mahimong black hole pagkahuman sa supernova! Ang gravity niini kaayo ka kusog nga bisan ang suga dili makalikyas sa event horizon.
evidence: "Tapak" means to step on or patch (zero corpus bodies use it for formation, and this card's own body says "pagporma"), so the headline reads "Stepping on the Black Hole".

fact_en: Three examples of igneous rock are granite, basalt, and obsidian!
fact_bis: Tulo ka pananglitan sa igneous rock mao ang granite, basalt, ug obsidian!
evidence: Last word "Igneo" is cut off; the card itself contains "Igneous".

fact_en:
Ever wonder how long a day really is?

Earth spins exactly once in about 24 hours, and that spin makes up the length of one full day!
fact_bis:
Nahibalo ka ba kung unsa ka dugay ang usa ka adlaw?

Ang Yuta motuyok kausa sulod sa mga 24 ka oras, ug mao kana ang gitas-on sa usa ka adlaw!
evidence: "Tirok" means to gather/congregate and appears in no Cebuano body in the corpus for rotation, while the body says "motuyok", so "24 Oras Tirok" reads as a 24-hour gathering rather than one spin.
